GK-01.c01: **CMV** = commercial motor vehicle, **CDL** = commercial driver license, and CLP = commercial learner's permit, the learning stage before the CDL.
**GVWR** is the loaded weight the manufacturer sets for one vehicle; **GCWR** is the loaded weight set for a combination (power unit plus towed unit).
No maker's GCWR → add the power unit's **GVWR** to the weight of the towed unit and its load.
An **endorsement** is an extra letter allowing special driving; a **restriction** is a code that limits what you may drive.
A **placarded load** is HazMat in an amount that requires diamond-shaped warning signs (placards) on the vehicle.
GK-01.c02: You need a CDL for a single vehicle with GVWR of **26,001 lb or more**, or a combination with GCWR of **26,001 lb or more**.
You need a CDL for a vehicle designed, used or maintained to carry **more than 10 people**, counting the driver.
You need a CDL to tow a vehicle or trailer with GVWR of **10,001 lb or more**, haul placarded HazMat, or tow two units at once.
[CA] A **3-axle** vehicle that weighs **more than 6,000 lb** also needs a CDL.
The lines sit one pound above a round number, so **26,000** or **10,000** is the trap answer.
GK-01.c03: [CA] Van with GCWR **more than 26,000 lb** → CDL required; used as a **vanpool** → no CDL.
[CA] Van carrying **more than 15** people including the driver → CDL required.
[CA] **More than 10** people including the driver → CDL only if it carries people **for pay or profit, or a nonprofit group uses it**.
Example: a nonprofit church van built for **12** people including the driver, not a vanpool → **CDL required**.
GK-01.c04: [CA] A horse trailer carries property; "living quarters" in it are only a side feature and do not change that.
[CA] A horse trailer with living quarters and GVWR **over 10,000 lb** needs a **commercial Class A** license.
[CA] If the truck-and-trailer GCWR is **under 26,001 lb**, DMV adds **Restriction 88**.
[CA] Restriction 88 → only combinations with GCWR **under 26,001 lb** whose towed vehicle has GVWR **over 10,000 lb**.
GK-01.c05: Combination with GCWR **26,001 lb or more** and towed unit GVWR 10,001 lb or more → **Class A**.
[CA] Combination with GCWR under 26,001 lb but towed unit GVWR 10,001 lb or more → **Class A with Restriction 88**.
Power unit GVWR **26,001 lb or more**, alone or towing under 10,001 lb → **Class B**; [CA] so is a single 3-axle vehicle over 6,000 lb.
Farm labor vehicle for **10 or more**, or **more than 10** people used for profit, pay or a nonprofit → Class B (counts include driver).
None of the above but carrying placarded HazMat → **Class C**; otherwise no CDL.
GK-01.c06: You must be at least **18** and already hold a valid California license covering at least noncommercial **Class C**; carry both.
A CLP lasts up to **180 days**, renewable for 180 more, but never past **1 year** from first application.
Only **N, P and S** endorsements go on a CLP; N means empty tanks only (purged if it held HazMat), P or S means no passengers.
Wait at least **14 days** after the CLP is first issued before the skills test.
A **CDL holder** with the right class and endorsements must ride with you whenever you drive a CMV.
GK-01.c07: [CA] Minimum CDL age is **18**, after first getting a California noncommercial Class C license.
[CA] From **18** you may drive **for hire inside California**, as long as you do no interstate commerce.
[CA] You must be **21** to drive in **interstate** commerce or haul HazMat or hazardous wastes, even on a trip inside California.
GK-01.c08: Bring **Form DL 44C**; signing it means agreeing to a chemical test for alcohol or drugs when a peace officer asks, and refusing means no license.
Bring an **identity document** as a **certified copy** proving birth date and legal presence; a photocopy is not accepted.
[CA] Bring **one residency document** whose address matches your DL 44C, for an original and each renewal, transfer or upgrade.
Prove your Social Security number; for an **original CDL** only the **Social Security card** is accepted.
Also bring your approved **medical forms**, the application fee, and a **DL 170 ETP** if your employer is authorized to issue one.
GK-01.c09: The application fee stays valid for **12 months** after the date you apply.
Knowledge tests → **3 attempts** per application, with **no waiting period** between them.
Skills tests → **3 attempts in total** per application, and **each failed part counts as 1**.
Skills parts you pass count only during the **first 180 days** of the CLP; after a renewal you retake all skills parts.
Failing basic control skills or the road test means a **retest fee** when you return.
GK-01.c10: Be a **California resident**, list every state that licensed you in the past **10 years**, and hand in all out-of-state licenses.
Tell your home state DMV about an out-of-state conviction, and your employer about any conviction (form **DL 535**), within **30 days**.
Tell your employer about a suspension, revocation, cancellation or disqualification before the **end of the next business day** (§1.4 says **2 business days**).
Give a new employer your **10-year** commercial driving work history; one driver, one license, one record.
GK-01.c11: H = HazMat (needs a **TSA background check**); N = tank, each tank **more than 119 gal** and all tanks 1,000 gal or more.
**P** = passenger vehicles built for **10 or more** people including driver; S = school buses, Class A or B only.
**T** = double or triple trailers, but [CA] **triple trailers are not legal in California**.
**X** = tank vehicles with placarded HazMat, showing you passed **both** the tank and HazMat tests.
[CA] **F** = firefighting equipment; required to drive it, **optional** for Class A or B holders.
GK-01.c12: Your CDL covers only what you proved on the skills test; there are **10** standard restriction codes.
**E** = no manual transmission; **L** = no air-brake CMV; Z = no full air-brake CMV (tested with air-over-hydraulic brakes).
**K** = intrastate only; **O** = no tractor-trailer (tested with a pintle hook or non-fifth-wheel hitch); V = medical variance.
**M** = no Class A passenger vehicle; **N** = no Class A or B passenger vehicle.
A CLP with P or S always gets restriction **P** (no passengers); a CLP with N always gets restriction **X** (no cargo in tank).
GK-01.c13: No CDL is needed for someone driving in an emergency **at a peace officer's direction**, or for **vanpool** drivers.
Towing, **not for pay**, a fifth-wheel travel trailer over **15,000 lb GVWR** or trailer coach over 10,000 lb GVWR needs only noncommercial Class A.
Housecar drivers **over 40 ft but not over 45 ft** (with an endorsement), non-civilian military drivers, and unlicensed farm-equipment operators are also exempt.
GK-01.c14: [CA] Some jobs need a certificate **in addition to** a CDL, such as ambulance, school bus, SPAB, transit, paratransit, farm labor and youth bus.
[CA] Non-work cell phone use while driving a **school bus or transit vehicle** is **illegal**; emergency calls are allowed.
[CA] HAM certificate lets a farm worker aged **21+** haul hazardous loads **without a CDL**, no more than 50 miles point to point.
[CA] School bus drivers **65+** send MER and MEC **every year**; ambulance drivers every 2 years.
GK-01.c15: You must pass **both** the knowledge and skills tests to get a CDL.
The handbook prepares you for the tests but does not replace a truck-driving school; DMV calls formal training the most dependable way to learn.
GK-01.c16: [CA] Knowledge tests come in **English, Arabic, Chinese, Punjabi, Russian and Spanish** on DMV's AKTE equipment.
Everyone takes **General knowledge**; air brakes (including **air-over-hydraulic**), combination, passenger, HazMat, tank, doubles/triples and school bus depend on your license.
Adding an endorsement without moving up a class → passed tests are waived if within **12 months** of your last renewal or original issue.
Allow **2–3 hours** to take all tests; tests are not returned to you.
GK-01.c17: Knowledge test → no notes, phone or watch; any aid or stand-in test taker means the test is **failed**.
Vehicle inspection test → the **only** aid allowed is the handbook's **Section 11 vehicle inspection guide**.
No electronic devices, bystander help or helper marks on the vehicle or curbs → test stopped and failed.
**No recording, including dash cams**; switch it off or block it during the road test, because the test must show what you know.
GK-01.c18: Skills tests come only **after** passing knowledge tests, in the vehicle type you want, **all in English** with no interpreter.
Three tests: vehicle inspection ~**40 min**, basic control skills ~**30 min**, road test ~45–60 min.
A road test is required for an **original** CDL, removing a size/equipment restriction, adding P or S, or renewing a CDL expired **more than 2 years**.
Troops to Trucks can **waive the skills test** for qualified military drivers, but **not** for S or P.
GK-01.c19: **Class A** → study Sections **1, 2, 3, 6** and 11–13, plus 5 for air brakes; Class B or C study the same without 6.
Endorsements add: passenger → **4**, doubles/triples → **7**, tank → 8 and 9 (plus 6 for Class B or C), HazMat → 9, school bus → 10.
GK-01.c20: Every CDL driver gives DMV a valid **MER** and **MEC**, both dated within the last 2 years; submit only MER pages 1–4.
Interstate CDL drivers must use a **National Registry** examiner; [CA] your employer pays if the job requires a CDL.
[CA] California has **no variances or exemptions** from the federal physical standards.
**Carry the MEC** whenever you drive commercially; driving after it expires can get you **cited for driving out of class**.
[CA] School bus drivers **65 or older** need a new medical report every year; mail updates at least **4 weeks** before expiration.
GK-01.c21: Federal rule makes you **self-certify** your type of commerce as interstate or intrastate.
Interstate commerce includes trips between two places in the same state as part of a shipment that **began or will end outside** the state.
You can be in **interstate** commerce even if your truck never leaves California.
**NI** is issued without limits; **NA** gets the Intrastate Only restriction 40/K; EI and EA are not issued in California.
DMV **strongly recommends NI** if you meet the federal qualifications and might ever drive interstate.
